key_insight: Micropillar compression reveals that anorthite deforms most easily by mechanical twinning, while slip strength depends strongly on temperature and crystal orientation.
engineering_relevance: These measurements provide quantitative crystal-plasticity parameters for plagioclase, improving constitutive models of crustal rheology and deformation prediction.
method: FIB-milled ~1 µm micropillars from three orientations of anorthite single crystals
Compressed 36 pillars in a SEM at 25, 300, and 800 °C
Extracted CRSS and yield stress for twinning and specific slip systems
evidence_signal: The study reports a CRSS of about 300 MPa for pericline twinning, with twinning nearly temperature- and strain-rate-insensitive and slip showing a strong temperature-dependent drop in yield stress.
watch_item: Micropillar results reflect small-scale, orientation-specific behavior and may not translate directly to bulk rock deformation under complex natural loading conditions.
paper_title: Quantification of plastic deformation in anorthite using micropillar compression
